name: hammurabi-code-penalties
description: A Babylonian king had a table of laws carved in stone, setting fixed punishments for crimes from theft to murder.

name: newgate-prison-built
description: A gatehouse in London's old city wall became a jail, starting centuries as the capital's most notorious prison.

name: bridewell-house-of-correction
description: A royal palace in London was given over to hold vagrants and petty offenders and set them to work, a model for later prisons.

name: paris-lieutenant-general-police
description: Louis XIV created a post to oversee the French capital's streets, lighting and order, giving Paris an early organised police.

name: bow-street-runners-formed
description: A London magistrate's small band of paid thief-takers began chasing offenders, an early step toward a professional police.

name: vidocq-founds-surete
description: A reformed criminal organised a plainclothes brigade using informers and records to catch thieves, ancestor of detective units.

name: last-public-hanging-england
description: A convicted murderer was hanged outside Newgate, the final execution held before a crowd; later ones moved behind prison walls.

name: bertillon-criminal-measurement
description: A Paris police clerk introduced body measurements and photographs to identify repeat offenders, a forerunner of forensic records.

name: first-electric-chair-execution
description: A New York murderer became the first person put to death by electric current, in a grim trial of a supposedly humane method.

name: scotland-yard-fingerprint-bureau
description: London's police adopted a filing system for fingerprints, replacing body measurements as the way to identify criminals.

name: wireless-catches-crippen
description: A ship's captain radioed Scotland Yard about a suspicious passenger couple, and a detective overtook them on a faster liner.

name: polygraph-invented
description: A California police officer and medical student built a device recording blood pressure and breathing to detect lies.

name: first-gas-chamber-execution
description: A Nevada prison put a convicted murderer to death with lethal gas, introducing a new method of capital punishment.

name: first-911-call
description: A phone call in a small Alabama town tested a single nationwide emergency number for police, fire and medical help.

name: first-lethal-injection-execution
description: A Texas prisoner became the first person executed by intravenous drugs, a method presented as more humane.

name: dna-evidence-convicts-killer
description: After mass testing of local men, a baker was convicted of two murders in the first case solved by DNA profiling.

name: golden-state-killer-identified
description: Investigators matched crime-scene DNA to relatives on a public ancestry database to arrest a suspect in decades-old cases.
